authority.scope: The authority comes from reviewed extension mock registration, not an actual Faux/provider wire capture. A future acceptor must bind and compare the real Context again.

evidence: EXPECTED_SCHEMA_SHA256 is the independent root-derived 553e00... authority, not a hash learned from either observed Context.

Before each response, canonicalToolSchema maps the complete ordered six-tool name/description/parameters array, recursively sorts object keys, preserves arrays, rejects nonfinite and non-JSON values, and requires its SHA-256 to equal the pinned authority.
After mocked main returns, exactly two observations must exist, be byte-identical, and each hash to the pinned authority before postflight or metadata publication.
Metadata publishes only the pinned authority hash after both checks; it cannot turn a self-observation into expected authority.
Exact wrong property type, reordered required array, changed description, and extra JSON Schema keyword all reject even when the same wrong Context would be used for both calls.

execution_boundary: Only the exact nine mocks and targeted TypeScript command ran. No publicMain/default Faux registration/stream, Bridge, process, fixture, Git, socket, ORX, Docker, provider, auth, raw data, model, combination case, or P0 executed. No source or production file was edited.

failing_first_archive.assessment: The stored four-schema red directly fails the property-type, required-array, description, and extra-keyword controls before the nine-test green; source/test/report snapshots match the reviewed bytes.

limits: publicMain, default registerFauxProvider, and Faux stream were not invoked; tests use an injected main, registration, ExtensionAPI, PreparedControllerMain, and metadata sink.
The post-return call-count guard is not a synchronous pre-request ceiling; no third response is queued and no fallback is configured.
Synthetic response IDs/metadata are not provider, OAuth, native usage, or execution evidence.
Passing this repair releases only the Faux source anchor to the acceptor, not a live case.
verified_controls: Exactly six ordered tool names and the fixed synthetic model/provider CLI binding are required before registration.
Exactly two fixed response factories and response IDs are used; the first is read_public_result({}) and the second is fixed text.
Fewer or more calls, pending responses, seventh tool, wrong model/tool CLI, and api-key/provider flags reject without fallback.
Prepared main arguments remain unchanged; one test-only provider factory is appended; registration always unregisters in finally.
Postflight precedes bounded metadata sink, and metadata stays explicitly test-only/NATIVE_SESSION_ONLY rather than provider or usage authority.
